help.content:
[b]GAN Organism Arena — handbook[/b]
The world begins with young aquatic organisms on a coast. Each has its own inherited material, energy reserves, senses and movement capabilities. Observe which descendants arise and survive in their environment. There is no prescribed evolutionary path or guaranteed future species.

[b]Move, select and follow[/b]
WASD and mouse move the camera; Q/E move down/up. Shift increases camera speed. The wheel zooms; Shift plus wheel adjusts camera movement speed. Left click selects the organism under the crosshair, Tab the next one. Right click toggles following. Follow placement accounts for terrain. Escape releases the mouse or first closes an open menu.

[b]Pause and menus[/b]
P, Space or the Pause key stops the world; press again to resume. Movement, ageing, energy use, growth, embryos, food renewal, water waves, automatic lighting and ongoing thought/audio output stop. Outside menus the camera remains usable for inspection. A yellow message identifies the pause. Paused wall-clock time is not caught up later.
F10 opens settings and F1 this handbook; both pause the world too. A manual pause stays set when menus close. Help opened from settings returns there. Deliberate settings changes and exports remain available. Interfaces can still observe but cannot bypass a local pause by advancing or changing the world. Pausing preserves an explicitly selected stepped experiment mode.

[b]Habitats, land, water and light[/b]
Keys 5–9 switch habitats; their names appear in the habitat option. The coast offers water, land and airspace. Numpad +/− changes world size. Each L press chooses a new light direction. The light option also offers fixed directions and an automatic sun.
Ancestors start in water. Inherited changes can enable other respiratory systems, limbs and support tissue. Land movement requires suitable physiology; flight also requires adequate body structure, lift, energy, development and sky. Carrying a genetic tendency alone does not grant a finished ability.

[b]Food, movement and survival[/b]
Organisms seek reachable food, explore and react to threats or partners. They retain goals for a while and replan after poor progress. Food is consumed within head reach. Strength, body size, covering and shape affect movement and costs. Oxygen, moisture, temperature and energy can constrain behaviour. Adapted individuals may leave more descendants; mutation can also be harmful.
Hunting, packs, hiding, filtering, parasitic feeding and tool use depend on suitable traits and conditions. Stationary feeding together with substrate anchoring can yield rooted aquatic or land forms. Trees also need structural support. Founders are not injected as ready-made plants or flyers.

[b]DNA, inheritance and new bodies[/b]
A genome holds two copies per regulatory locus. Its 91 loci influence proportions, support, muscles, respiration, coverings and behaviour. Sexual offspring receive one copy from egg and sperm; meiosis exchanges parental chromosome segments. Clonal reproduction copies both homologs.
Small and major regulatory mutations change individual copies while retaining their counterparts. Some changes remain latent and may combine in later generations. Hue, saturation and brightness are inherited too. Learned memories are not written into the germ line. DNA export maps loci and actual new allele changes. This fictional code does not implement real protein synthesis.
The body generator has seven basic topologies with continuous variations. Descendants can look very different from their ancestors. A topology is not a scientific species definition, and the generator’s geometry grammar remains finite.

[b]Cell division, reproduction and development[/b]
Mitosis supports tissue growth, repair and, in suitable lineages, clonal reproduction. Meiosis produces haploid gametes for sexual reproduction. Combined strategies are possible. A mature organism still needs compatible reproductive roles, usable anatomy and enough energy or gamete reserves.
Traits can support external spawning, egg laying, retained eggs, live birth or clonal propagation. Courtship and contact precede possible fertilization. Embryos need resources and time, may fail and reserve population slots. Young grow through stages; suitable development can include larvae or pupae. Hunger and low oxygen slow growth. Disabling new reproduction does not stop existing embryos developing.

[b]Population and replacements[/b]
Automatic replacement targets at least five living organisms by default. Missing places are filled with unrelated aquatic young with random genes, including after extinction. Population capacity and embryo reservations limit refill. The overview shows any deficit. Disable replacement to allow complete extinction. New reproduction has a separate switch. G manually introduces a founder if room is available.

[b]Views and evolutionary observations[/b]
Keys 1–4 show natural bodies, cells/tissues, neural structures and energy. Selection details include life stage, parents, energy, oxygen, reproductive state, anatomy and navigation goals. Body and mind scores are internal comparison values, not centimetres or IQ. Thoughts describe modelled states. Display and spoken language can be selected separately; speech needs a matching installed system voice.
F10’s overview separates natural sexual/clonal offspring from automatic/manual introductions. It shows generations, deaths, rooted organisms, first new topologies and recent parentage. A previously injected topology does not count as a subsequent evolutionary discovery.

[b]Performance and contact accuracy[/b]
For low frame rates, first lower contact accuracy, visible body-cell count or population capacity. Lower contact accuracy saves computation but permits more small overlaps. Higher simulation tick rates refine decisions and cost CPU time. Visual detail and morphology rebuild intervals affect other costs. Offscreen visual work is reduced while biology continues. A different renderer needs a restart; try the Compatibility launcher if needed.

[b]Profiles, exports and a new world[/b]
Settings profiles save/load options, not a world state. DNA export saves the selected genome; F8 exports its current OBJ geometry; F12 takes a screenshot. Evolution export saves observations and up to 2,048 genealogy records as JSON. Discarded older records are reported and totals survive eviction. It is not a reloadable world save either. Resetting the world begins a new run and recording.

[b]Optional AI interfaces[/b]
MCP and VKLP can be enabled independently and are off by default. Normal use needs no AI connection. Connected systems can observe and run explicit experiments; supplied information can support logged parameter changes. Connecting alone does not reset the world. Separate VKLP write permission governs submissions. Local pauses take priority. Exports include model assumptions so observations stay attributable to their fictional experiment.

The reference below explains every option and button individually.

[b]Complete key reference[/b]
W/S or Up/Down move forward/back; A/D or Left/Right strafe; Q/E move down/up; mouse movement looks around. Shift accelerates movement. Wheel zooms; Shift+wheel adjusts movement speed. Left click selects, Tab selects the next organism, right click follows. P/Space/Pause pauses. 1–4 select natural/cell/neural/energy views. 5–9 select habitats. Numpad +/− resizes the world. G introduces a founder. L randomizes light. F1 opens help, F2 hides/shows the HUD, F8 exports OBJ, F9 reloads enabled PNG templates, F10 opens settings, F12 saves a screenshot. Escape closes a panel or releases/recaptures the mouse.

tooltips.language: Language of menus, status text and organism thoughts. Applied immediately.
tooltips.speech_language: Language used for spoken thoughts; follow uses the menu language. Requires an installed matching system voice.
tooltips.tts_voice: Choose an installed voice for the speech language. Automatic selects a matching voice; a missing voice never falls back to another language.
tooltips.mcp_enabled: Allow local AI clients to observe and control this world through the optional MCP adapter. Switching off rejects further access. Connecting does not reset the world.
tooltips.vklp_enabled: Allow the optional VKLP client to exchange world evidence and documented knowledge. Direct VKLP also works with MCP off. No automatic network requests.
tooltips.vklp_write_enabled: Additionally permit explicitly requested claim submissions to the configured VKLP ledger. Reading alone does not require this permission.
tooltips.vklp_url: Base URL of your VKLP service, for example http://127.0.0.1:8000. Remote services require HTTPS. Keep the API key in the VKLP_API_KEY environment variable.
tooltips.renderer: Graphics backend used after the next restart. Compatibility can help on older graphics hardware.
tooltips.auto_reseed: Continuously restores a declining or already empty population to the selected target with genetically random aquatic hatchling founders. Turn it off to allow extinction.
tooltips.minimum_population: Number of living organisms maintained while automatic reseed is on (default 5). The effective target cannot exceed the population cap; embryos do not count as living organisms.
tooltips.fullscreen: Switch between fullscreen and a window without restarting the simulation.
tooltips.view_mode: Display natural tissues, separated cells, nervous tissue or energy colors. Biology and collisions use the same body in every view.
tooltips.light_mode: Direction of scene lighting. Automatic follows the sun; random chooses a new direction. The L key randomizes it directly.
tooltips.simulation_speed: How quickly simulated time passes compared with real time. Higher speeds increase the work per frame.
tooltips.simulation_tick_hz: Biological decision updates per simulated second. Higher values improve temporal detail and cost more CPU time.
tooltips.evolution_rate: Multiplier for within-life complexity and cognition development. Hereditary variation is controlled separately by mutation and crossing options.
tooltips.habitat_level: Choose habitat 5–9, from water to coast and sky. Changes available environments and abilities such as flight.
tooltips.world_step: Size increment used by NumPad plus/minus when resizing the world.
tooltips.organism_cap: Maximum living population plus reserved offspring slots. Lowering it prevents additional births until room is available.
tooltips.nutrient_count: Number of finite food particles in the world. Changing this rebuilds the nutrient field and changes food availability.
tooltips.visual_cell_cap: Maximum tissue cells per organism, plus at most one connecting segment per cell. Higher values show more anatomy and cost more rendering time.
tooltips.body_rebuild_interval: Seconds between checks for grown or changed anatomy. Joint animation continues between rebuilds.
tooltips.mutation_strength: Magnitude of small inherited allele changes. Zero disables small mutations. Also set major-mutation probability to zero to disable all new mutations.
tooltips.macro_mutation_rate: Chance of a major regulatory mutation per offspring. Each affected locus changes one homolog, preserving the other. The mutation may remain latent without changing the visible body immediately.
tooltips.crossover_rate: Frequency of attempted sexual crossing, subject to maturity, compatibility and available gametes.
tooltips.viability_threshold: Minimum developmental stability required for reproduction. Low stability also reduces early survival.
tooltips.mate_cooldown: Recovery time in simulated seconds after reproduction before another attempt is possible.
tooltips.mating_radius: Distance within which a compatible partner can be found. Fertilization still requires physical contact or the appropriate spawning/pollination route.
tooltips.social_spacing: Preferred spacing in ordinary social movement. The body-contact solver separately prevents penetration.
tooltips.courtship_strength: How strongly compatible partners approach during courtship. Does not bypass biological compatibility.
tooltips.group_strength: Strength of cohesion and coordinated movement for organisms with social traits.
tooltips.predation_strength: Intensity of hunting and feeding interactions, still limited by anatomy, energy and available prey.
tooltips.hierarchy_strength: Influence of social rank on movement near other organisms.
tooltips.follow_distance: Distance behind the selected organism when following with the camera.
tooltips.follow_height: Height of the following camera above its target.
tooltips.camera_noclip: Allows the observer camera to pass through terrain and mountains. World boundaries still apply; turn it off for terrain-aware movement and following.
tooltips.observer_presence: Adds a virtual adult human-like observer signal. Sensitive organisms can look at, approach or avoid the observer; it is never treated as food or a mate.
tooltips.show_hud: Shows or hides status, selection and thought text during normal viewing. The settings and help panels remain available through F10 and F1.
tooltips.show_crosshair: Shows or hides the centre aiming marker used for left-click organism selection. Hiding it does not disable selection or Tab navigation.
tooltips.camera_fov: Camera field of view in degrees. Smaller values zoom in; larger values show more surroundings.
tooltips.zoom_step: Change in field of view per mouse-wheel notch while looking around.
tooltips.audio_enabled: Master switch for environmental and organism sounds. Spoken thoughts have their own thought-mode setting.
tooltips.ambient_audio: Enable background habitat sounds when audio is enabled.
tooltips.organism_audio: Enable nonverbal calls of the organisms. This is separate from spoken thought narration.
tooltips.audio_volume: Volume of habitat sounds and nonverbal organism calls.
tooltips.organism_sound_interval: Minimum interval between sampled organism calls; longer intervals make the soundscape quieter.
tooltips.thought_mode: Off, on-screen text, spoken narration or both. The language stage of each organism determines its vocabulary.
tooltips.thought_interval: Seconds between displayed or spoken thoughts. Does not alter organism decision frequency.
tooltips.max_history_events: Maximum remembered events per organism used when composing thoughts. Older events are discarded first.
tooltips.save_settings: Save all current options as a named JSON profile. This saves settings, not organisms or world progress.
tooltips.load_settings: Choose a JSON settings profile. The complete file is validated before application; invalid files leave current settings unchanged.
tooltips.test_speech: Speak a short sample using the selected language and installed voice.
tooltips.rebuild_visuals: Immediately rebuild all organism anatomy and render resources from current genes and life stages.
tooltips.inject: Introduce a new aquatic founder into the current world, subject to the population limit.
tooltips.export_selected: Export the selected body as an OBJ mesh for inspection in a 3D application.
tooltips.reset_world: Replace the current population and world with a new simulation. Existing organisms and world progress are lost.
tooltips.close_settings: Close this panel and return to the simulation with the current settings.
tooltips.export_genome: Save paired fictional DNA chromosomes with mapped gene locations, complementary strands and genome metadata as JSON.
tooltips.contact_quality: 0–100: Lower values allow slight overlap and limit body contact correction passes. Below 90, ground support uses the centre of each body part; from 90, four footprint edges are also tested. 100 gives the highest accuracy at greater CPU cost. Default: 85. Applies immediately and is saved in settings profiles. The number is a quality level, not an accuracy percentage.
tooltips.gravity_scale: Sets gravitational acceleration from 0.2× to 2.5× Earth gravity. Changes falling, ballistic jump height, buoyancy forces and the lift needed for flight; 1.0 is the default. Applies immediately and is saved in settings profiles.
tooltips.auto_reproduce: Allows new courtship, fertilization and clonal reproduction. Existing embryos keep developing when switched off. Independent of automatic population replacement.
tooltips.evolution_overview: Shows natural and clonal births, introduced founders, generations, rooted organisms, recent parentage and the first appearance of new body topologies in this run.
tooltips.export_evolution: Saves evolutionary counters and up to 2,048 birth/death genealogy records as JSON in exports/evolution. Reports discarded history; this is not a reloadable world save.
tooltips.show_help: Opens the full guide to controls, the living world, inheritance, developmental stages, every option and exports. Closing it returns to settings while the world remains paused.
tooltips.textures_enabled: Loads replaceable terrain and organism PNG files. Off by default. When enabled, every child receives a new pixel mixture made from the actual parent coat images; existing descendants retain their inherited pattern.
tooltips.reload_textures: Reloads the replaceable PNG templates from the textures subfolders. Existing inherited organism coats stay unchanged; the terrain and newly created founders use the replacements.
tooltips.export_texture: Writes the selected organism’s generated inherited coat pattern to exports/textures as a PNG file. Requires optional textures to be enabled.
tooltips.plant_evolution_bias: Makes the rooted-plant niche easier or harder to discover. It lowers the inherited anchoring and stationary-food thresholds, but never roots aquatic founders on spawn.
tooltips.exit_open_settings: Closes this prompt and opens the full options panel; the simulation remains paused.
tooltips.exit_save_quit: Writes a complete JSON observation snapshot, including organisms, DNA, nutrients, remains and camera state, then exits.
tooltips.exit_quit: Exits immediately without writing a world snapshot.
tooltips.exit_cancel: Closes this prompt and returns to the previous view without changing the world.

evolution.discovery_note: Counts the first appearance of a body topology in this run, not a biological species. Earlier manual injections also count as already known. Inherited shape variation remains possible within each topology.

evolution.retention: Retained birth records: %d. Older records discarded: %d. Totals and first discoveries survive eviction. Export contains the retained genealogy; it is an observation, not a world save.
